text:
Situation: Potassium chloride has been on FDA's shortage list since 2019-06-10 with a status of To Be Discontinued. As of 2026-10-21 the shortage has been listed for 88 months. Current inventory across Corvale sites shows days on hand ranging from 2.7 days for the 29.8G/50ML bag at Corvale East to 22 days for 750MG tablets at Corvale East. Multiple presentations are below 10 days supply at East and Lakeside locations.

Why (FDA record): FDA inspection 985599 at Baxter Healthcare Corporation (FEI 2618677) ended 2016-10-03 and was classified OAI, 980 days before FDA posted the potassium chloride shortage on 2019-06-10. Additional OAI classifications at the same plant occurred in 2010, 2013, 2014, and 2015, with VAI inspections in 2018 and 2024. A second Baxter plant (FEI 1416980) received OAI classifications in 2024 and 2026, followed by a Warning Letter on 2026-09-29. Pfizer Healthcare India Private Limited (FEI 3008316085) received an OAI classification in 2019 and a Warning Letter in 2020. Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1021343) had multiple OAI inspections between 2010 and 2011 with a Warning Letter in 2010.

Our position: Supply is critically low for several potassium chloride presentations, particularly IV bags at Corvale East and Lakeside. The rule-selected alternate manufacturer A-S Medication Solutions is not on FDA's shortage list today but its label names no plant we could place. Four additional manufacturers (Advagen Pharma Limited, Affordable Pharmaceuticals LLC, Ajenat Pharmaceuticals LLC, American Health Packaging) are also not on FDA's shortage list but similarly lack identifiable plant information on their labels.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to initiate emergency purchase from A-S Medication Solutions for potassium chloride IV presentations; requires Pharmacy Director approval.
2. Buyer to qualify Advagen Pharma Limited as secondary source; requires Pharmacy Director and P&T Committee Chair approval.
3. Buyer to evaluate Affordable Pharmaceuticals LLC, Ajenat Pharmaceuticals LLC, and American Health Packaging for formulary addition; requires P&T Committee approval.
4. Buyer to request allocation data from current distributors for all potassium chloride presentations; requires Supply Chain Manager approval.
5. Buyer to report weekly inventory status to Pharmacy Director until all presentations exceed 14 days supply at all sites; requires Pharmacy Director approval.

Not recommended: Switching patients to alternative potassium salts or changing dosing regimens; clinical changes are for the treating clinicians and the committee.
